questions.function: CAN controller clock (the crystal, resonator or oscillator each controller takes)
questions.question: What load capacitance in pF, highest ESR in Ohm, lowest drive-level rating in uW, highest shunt capacitance C0 in pF, and which cut and mode must a crystal or resonator for the CAN controller's 40 MHz clock meet, and what supply voltage, output type/logic level and current must an oscillator meet instead, to drive the MCP2518FD's OSC1/OSC2 pins?
questions.why: P2 cannot qualify a candidate crystal, resonator or oscillator without these electrical limits; neither IOBoard.md's Controller clock and Clock accuracy rows, Pins.md:160-161 nor the Round 2 Follow-ups row (Research.md:570) state any of them, unlike R1's equivalent 12 MHz crystal, which has this exact class of value raised and answered as V6 (load capacitance, ESR, drive level) and V15 (shunt capacitance C0, cut and mode).

questions.function: onboard pack switch MOSFETs; external pack switch module; pack overvoltage and transient clamp
questions.question: What ambient temperature range, in degC, and supply range, in V, must the replacement onboard MOSFET array, the external module and the overvoltage/transient clamp hold their safe-operating-area, turn-off and clamp figures across? Monostable.md's step 11 corner sweep (0 to 50 degC, 3.2-3.4 V) explicitly repeats only steps 7 and 10, the window's own timing tests; step 9, 'The switches and the rails', is not in that list, so the corner sweep does not qualify the switches, and V38 (R3, monostable), which asks the identical question for 'the safety gate and the ESC pack switches', is still unanswered.
questions.why: P2 cannot qualify a replacement MOSFET array, module or clamp on safe operating area and thermal rise without a stated ambient/supply range; P1's value (index 35) marks the window's corner sweep as extending 'by extension' to the gates it drives, but Monostable.md step 11 names only steps 7 and 10, not step 9, so that extension is unsupported and the underlying need (V38) remains open.
questions.for_quantity: ambient/supply corners the window (and by extension the gates it drives) are qualified over

questions.question: Does the phase-wire clip's rpm reading divide by MOTOR_POLES / 2, as the ESC telemetry's 'Rotation from the ESC' conversion does (dividing the DShot reply's electrical period by MOTOR_POLES / 2), or does it already report mechanical rpm?

values.quantity: clock tolerance responsibility

values.refutation_tried: Checked against IOBoard.md:168 (Bit timing: exactly 1 Mbit/s) and IOBoard.md:199 (Controller clock: makes 1 Mbit/s exactly). The controller's clock accuracy sets whether the nominal bit time comes out exact, so the row's framing holds.

values.quantity: CAN controller clock frequency
values.value: each MCP2518FDT-E/SL, the link's and the external CAN port's, takes a 40 MHz clock (owner, 2026-10-01)
values.source: IOBoard.md:199 (Controller clock row); reason at hardware/docs/Pins.md:160-161: the MCP2518FD limits its SPI clock to 0.85 x SYSCLK / 2, so the link's 10 MHz SPI needs a 40 MHz system clock
values.refutation_tried: 0.85 x 40 / 2 = 17 MHz >= the 10 MHz SPI rate the link uses (IOBoard.md:200, Controller interface). Arithmetic supports 40 MHz as sufficient, but a lower frequency (e.g. 24 MHz, giving 10.2 MHz) would also clear that bound, so the specific 40 MHz figure is the owner's choice, not the only value the arithmetic forces. Consistent, not refuted.

At 10,000 rpm the period is 6,000 µs; 1°/360 x 6,000 µs = 16.67 µs, matching the stated 16.7 µs. Both follow correctly from the 1° figure and the rpm-to-period conversion; this total is an owner decision recorded with a date on the page, not an assumption. The owner's text leaves the three-way split (accelerometer, optical-index front end, converter) unstated beyond noting the converter's share is 'inside it'.

values.source: hardware/docs/Research.md:586 (Follow-ups row, source cited there as 'V225; Sensing.md, Not known'); hardware/docs/Sensing.md:118 (Not known); hardware/research/round1/FU-C2/002-P2-R11.json lines 106, 184, 511 (the 3-way split: 1.244 µs each to the accelerometer and the optical index, 55 ns to the index comparator, 30 ps to the converter, attributed there to 'the owner's decision on V225 of 2026-09-29 carried in this follow-up task's items and not on the page')

The 1.244 µs figure requires an additional, unequal split (2.543 µs minus the converter's 30 ps and the index comparator's 55 ns, the remaining 2.488 µs then divided evenly between the accelerometer and the optical index) that round 1's P2 return attributes to an owner decision dated 2026-09-29 -- but that decision carries no V-number, is not listed under Raised by P1 or Decided on the research's output, and the same JSON that cites it says it is 'not on the page'. Per the task's own rule that a proposed answer is not an answer, this split is not confirmed on either page and is marked an assumption here. The total (2.543 µs) is sourced/owner; the specific 1.244 µs allocated to the optical index is not.
